In the Data For Good generative AI white paper, the initial estimated carbon footprint for training the BLOOM model was 30 tonnes CO2eq (based on 433 MWh energy consumption and carbon intensity of 57 g CO2eq/kWh). When extending the scope to include additional factors such as the consumption of all data center equipment (increasing energy consumption from 433 MWh to 690 MWh), the impact of server manufacturing (considering a 6-year lifespan and manufacturing emissions), and the development phase (including tests, evaluations, and corrections), the estimated carbon footprint increased significantly.

Specifically, the impact of training alone rose from 39.3 tonnes CO2eq (after adjusting for additional equipment consumption) to 50.5 tonnes CO2eq when including manufacturing impacts. Adding the development phase added another 73.32 tonnes CO2eq. The total full-scope estimate of BLOOM's carbon footprint for training and development reached 123.82 tonnes CO2eq, which is about four times higher than the initial naive estimate.

Thus, BLOOM's estimated training carbon footprint changed from an initial estimate of approximately 30 tonnes CO2eq to a full-scope estimate of 123.82 tonnes CO2eq after including additional data center equipment, manufacturing impacts, and development phase emissions.
